title: Ganga in a cobbler's bowl
hookLine: a shoemaker at his bench is invited to the holy river, and stays
carry: if the mind is pure, the ganga is here
tomorrow: Why keep a lamp lit all night?

cards: A small shop in Banaras. The smell of leather, a low bench, a man bent over a shoe with an awl in his hand. This is Ravidas, the cobbler-saint, whom this path first met on day ninety-five.
A neighbor leans in the doorway. It's a holy day, he says. Everyone's going down to the Ganga to bathe.
Come with us. Ravidas looks at the shoe in his hands. In one telling, he has promised it to a customer by tonight.
Today, a cobbler who has to decide whether to put down his work.

teach.h: IF THE MIND IS PURE, THE GANGA IS HERE
teach.b: Here's the story people tell. Ravidas doesn't go. He tells his neighbor, in a line people still quote: if the mind is pure, the Ganga is in this bowl, the leatherworker's bowl of water by his bench.

In some tellings he gives the neighbor a coin to offer the river, but only if the Ganga reaches out and takes it herself. At the river, the story says, a hand rises from the water and takes it. First, the bench.
The story isn't against pilgrimage. Ravidas honors the Ganga; that's why the coin goes.

teach.h: A PURE HEART, NOT BIRTH OR PLACE
teach.b: What it teaches is one of bhakti's biggest ideas: what brings a person near God is a pure heart and love, not birth, caste or place.
Ravidas was born into a leatherworking caste that others treated as untouchable, and still the river came to his bench. Then, the song.
His hymns are kept in the Guru Granth Sahib, and in one he sings of a city called Begampura, the town without sorrow.

In paraphrase: no one there is anxious or afraid, no tax weighs on anyone, no one is ranked second or third, and anyone may walk where they please. A world where the cobbler and everyone else stand as equals.

teach.h: HONORED IN PUNJAB IN MANY WAYS
teach.b: Last, Punjab. Ravidas lived in Banaras, but in Punjab you'll hear him called Guru Ravidas, and his birthday is kept with processions and hymn singing.
Hindus honor him, Sikhs sing his hymns from their scripture, and communities who take his name honor him as their own Guru. Each comes to him in its own way.
And the week behind: a greeting, a letter, a company, a song, a kite string, a cobbler's bowl. Every one brings God into an ordinary day.

how: Ravidas's hymns are sung in gurdwaras from the Guru Granth Sahib and in Ravidas temples, and his birthday is kept in Punjab and beyond with processions and kirtan.

games.q: what does “punjab's shared devotional ground” mean?
o: Ravidas, the cobbler of Banaras who is honored in Punjab
a guild of leatherworkers that ran Punjab's markets
a river festival when all of Banaras bathes in the Ganga

p: where the Ganga is, if the mind is pure
taken by a hand from the river

s: the story mocks pilgrimage to the Ganga
Ravidas honors the river and sends a coin; the story says the holy reaches his bench too.
Ravidas's hymns are kept in the Guru Granth Sahib
including his song of Begampura, the town without sorrow.
in Punjab, only one community honors Ravidas
Hindus, Sikhs and communities who take his name each honor him in their own way.

games.q: you're Ravidas. it's a holy day, your neighbor is off to bathe in the Ganga, and you promised a shoe by tonight. what do you do?
o: drop the shoe and go to the river.
stay at the bench and keep your promise.
go, and tell the customer it's God's fault.
games.why: in the story he stays: if the mind is pure, the Ganga is in this bowl. and at the river, a hand rises to take his coin.

practice: Rest your hands where your work happens, on a desk, a counter or your knees, and think of the work in front of you this week, cooking, code, care, cleaning: let it be the bench.
For a few breaths, treat this place as enough; if you pray, offer that work to God as it is, here, without going anywhere.

wordCard.voice: Punjab's shared devotional ground. Today, Ravidas, the cobbler of Banaras honored in Punjab: a pure heart, not birth or place, brings God near. Today's word.

orig.note: the town without sorrow, the city Ravidas sings of in the Guru Granth Sahib.

carryVoice: Your line: if the mind is pure, the Ganga is here. The river can reach a cobbler's bench. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: the saying and story 'man changa to kathauti mein Ganga' (a story people tell about Ravidas)
